completed: Native agent configuration and budget-free execution

results.title: Native agent configuration and budget-free execution
results.summary: Removed the application budget subsystem: services, the reservation model and factory, the allowance columns and table (through a forward migration that classifies legacy pauses and keeps generation IDs), the Budget permission and policy, and the top-up UI and allowance copy. Each of the nine role agents now sets its own model, reasoning effort and token limit, validated against a small allowlist in config, with optional per-role overrides and a paused-by-default flag stored in Spatie settings (paused is checked when work starts, is approved, is resumed, runs or is recovered). Execution keeps its transactional pre-call and post-call freshness checks, records the chosen model in model_snapshot, pins Auto approval continuations to the concrete model or pauses, and pauses with fixed messages on rejected, uncertain or failed-continuation calls. Validation passes: the listed suites have 267 tests and the full suite 433; pint, phpstan, the bun tests, the build and git diff --check are all clean. Notes: record-rule appended a duplicate rule section, which was removed so one rule remains. ReleaseReadinessTest, the dashboard copy and tests/Pest.php were changed although the spec does not list them. The spec's research section records the 2026-09-25 catalog recheck. The untracked .impeccable/ files are someone else's changes and were not touched. — The implementation closely follows the Phase 1 spec. Each agent declares its model through a native `model()` method; the curated allowlist and scoped Spatie settings start paused; `provider.only` and `max_price` pins are gone while `require_parameters` stays; the pre- and post-call freshness checks were kept as `passesExecutionChecks()`; Auto approvals continue on the concrete returned model; and the forward migration preserves generation IDs and only reclassifies positively identified pre-call pauses. The tests are strong and use the concrete request bodies. The two medium findings are about how the reject-only continuation path and the new configuration pauses are classified and recovered, and neither blocks the commit, so it is ready to commit.
findings: medium/logic app/Actions/Publishing/RunEditorialActivity.php:69 — The all-reject approval continuation sends a paid provider request (`$agent->prompt($decisions)`) before `confirmBeforeInvocation()` runs and while `$invoked` is still false. That skips the transactional recheck the spec requires immediately before HTTP, and it never writes the execution snapshot. If this request times out or the provider rejects it, `handleFailure()` treats it as a pre-invocation failure and pauses with the raw exception text. Laravel's RequestException message includes the provider response body, which conflicts with the spec's failure policy of concise errors that never echo secrets. → Move the all-reject branch after `confirmBeforeInvocation()` and set `$invoked = true` before that prompt, so rejections, timeouts and 401/402 errors go through the same status-mapped failure handling as every other paid call.

medium/logic app/Actions/Publishing/RunEditorialActivity.php:464 — New pre-invocation failures (invalid saved override, recommended model missing from the allowlist, missing credentials) pause the activity with reasons that are not in `EditorialActivity::RESUMABLE_PAUSE_REASONS`. Once an activity is paused this way it cannot be resumed through the attempt, and `StartEditorialActivity` returns that same paused activity again through its idempotency key. So the message 'Reset it in the publishing agent settings' promises a fix that does not actually unblock the work. This is the same trap the budget-removal migration has to reclassify for legacy pre-call blockers. → Give positively identified pre-call configuration pauses a stable, resumable reason (or add them to RESUMABLE_PAUSE_REASONS), and add a test showing that resetting the override or restoring the key and then resuming the attempt returns the activity to pending.

low/logic app/Settings/PublishingAgentSettings.php:178 — `modelOverrideFor()` assumes every stored value is a string. A malformed payload value such as an array or null raises a TypeError instead of the actionable 'Reset it' error. → Check `is_string($override) && $override !== ''` before returning, so malformed values fall through to the allowlist validation in `configuredAgent()`.

low/testing tests/Feature/Publishing/PublishingAgentSettingsTest.php — No test covers a 429 or failure on the all-reject continuation path, or an invalid override stored for the continuation role. The failure classification of that branch is untested. → Add a case that fails a reject-only continuation and asserts the paused reason is status-mapped and contains no provider body.

results.title: Publishing settings and operational integration
results.summary: Added the gated Publishing Settings page (resources/views/components/admin/publishing/⚡settings.blade.php, route admin.publishing.settings). It has a pause switch with a separate saved-state badge and one explicit Save, a notice that only says whether an OpenRouter key is configured, and nine per-task model rows showing the code recommendation, pinned or reset-required state, and a reset. Access needs the new publishing.configure-agents permission, granted through the Author role and checked in mount and in every action, and a Settings link appears in the Publishing nav for those users. I rewrote the budget and PUBLISHING_AGENTS_* guidance in both setup docs, DESIGN.md and the surface brief, and recorded a settings rule with record-rule. All validation commands pass. The full suite also passes except 5 homepage MarketingSiteTest failures, which come from another session's in-progress, uncommitted edits to resources/views/pages/index.blade.php and the homepage assets, not from this phase. I added three changes outside the spec's file list: (1) resources/views/layouts/admin.blade.php hides the header 'Publishing' label below the sm breakpoint, because the third nav item made the header overflow at 390px; (2) a Livewire continuity test in EditorialToolApprovalTest.php, so it can reuse the pendingAuthorInterview helper; (3) .ai/rules/settings.md and its index row, from record-rule. PublishingAgentSettings.php, PublishingSessionTest.php and .impeccable/design.json needed no change (the design file has no allowance text). I did not migrate the local PostgreSQL DB, and the Playwright MCP browser was in use by another session. Rendered QA instead used an in-memory SQLite fixture with the real built assets in headless Chromium, with every POST blocked. At 1440 and 390px in light and dark it showed no overflow and no console errors, a switch→selects→Save tab order with visible focus, and working unsaved-change indicators; screenshots are in the gitignored .impeccable/review/publishing-settings/. It did not cover a real authenticated save or reset round-trip, or validation errors shown in the browser; the Livewire tests cover those. — Phase 2 follows the spec. ConfigureAgents is registered in the catalog and granted only through publishing.author. The route middleware checks it, and the component checks it again in mount, save and resetRole. The settings page shows only a boolean for credentials, strictly validates role and model keys, takes recommendations from the agent code, and removes an override when you pick 'Use recommended' or reset. Tests cover forged and revoked permissions, tampered input, secret redaction, settings reaching the next job without a restart, and approval continuations keeping their original model; the runbooks now describe the new behavior instead of the old budget setup. Nothing blocks the commit (all four findings are medium or low). The one condition is that the unrelated marketing work in the working tree stays unstaged, and the browser QA evidence is not visible in the diff, so it has to come from the builder's report.
findings: medium/spec-deviation resources/views/pages/index.blade.php:1 — The working tree also holds a marketing redesign that is not part of Phase 2: resources/views/pages/index.blade.php, resources/css/app.css (imports untracked home.css and adds a Mona Sans font token), resources/js/app.js (imports untracked miniature.js), vite.config.js (Mona Sans), PRODUCT.md, .impeccable/surfaces/resources-views-pages-index-blade-php.md and .impeccable/mocks/*. The spec forbids marketing changes. If app.css or app.js is committed without the untracked files, `bun run build` breaks. → When committing Phase 2, stage only the phase files: the settings SFC, routes/admin.php, navigation, layouts/admin.blade.php, the Authorization Catalog/Permission, the five tests, the two setup docs, DESIGN.md, the publishing surface brief, .ai/rules/settings.md, the .ai/rules/index.md row and the ideation context-map. Leave the marketing WIP unstaged.

low/spec-deviation resources/views/layouts/admin.blade.php:47 — This file is not in the spec's File Changes. The change hides the 'Publishing' shell label below sm on every publishing route, so it touches the existing workspace pages as well as Settings. It is a reasonable fix for fitting a third tab at 390px, but it was not declared. → Keep the change and name it in the phase handoff or commit body as the mobile-fit adjustment for the Settings tab, and confirm the 390px workspace header in the rendered pass.

low/spec-deviation docs/development-setup.md:305 — Spec step 5 asks the docs to explain bounded rate-limit retries. The 429 troubleshooting text in both runbooks (also docs/production-setup.md:334) only says the activity is marked failed and not retried automatically. It leaves out that RunEditorialActivity::failOrPause moves the activity to Paused once run_count exceeds limits.max_retries (2), so manual reruns are bounded. → Add one clause saying reruns of a rate-limited activity are bounded, and that it pauses for review after the retry limit.

low/testing tests/Feature/Publishing/PublishingAgentSettingsTest.php:save — The Throwable catch in save() that shows the 'Settings were not saved' callout has no test, so the failure feedback path is only covered if the browser pass reaches it. → Optionally add a Livewire test that forces the settings save to throw, then asserts the callout text and that the draft state is unchanged.
